module purpose: neorv32_bus provides several bus-control entities that arbitrate between requesters, optionally register request and response channels, decode and steer requests to downstream ports and devices, monitor bus timeouts, and implement atomic AMO RMW and LR/SC behavior.

use-case flows.value: arbitrate between A and B requests, remember pending requests, drive the selected request toward x_req_o, and route x_rsp_i back to the selected requester
remember lock state and keep a granted or monitored transaction active until the lock is released or the implemented release condition occurs
optionally register bus requests and responses between host and device sides
decode request addresses to downstream ports or devices, gate request strobes to the selected destination, and OR responses back
raise a timeout error response when an outstanding gateway request exceeds the implemented counter limit outside the halt path

sequence atomic read-modify-write operations by capturing the command and operand, waiting for read acknowledgment, computing the write-back value, issuing the write, and returning the saved read data
recognize LR/SC reservation operations, track reservation state, suppress or forward the store-conditional strobe accordingly, and report store-conditional failure
clear arbitration, monitor, buffering, and atomic-operation state to their defined reset values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Switch arbitration context -- stored pending requests, current and previous selection, and issued strobe that decide which requester is serviced
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 58-67 clear or latch the pending-request bits a_req and b_req while one side is busy, lines 83-130 derive sel, stb, and state_nxt from state, sel_q, and the pending requests, and lines 140-158 plus 164-169 use sel and stb to forward the chosen request and return ack/err to the chosen side. Integrity is established because corrupting this context would misroute or drop a request; availability is also established because a_req and b_req preserve a request until the corresponding busy path clears it (59, 64) or the idle branch services it (113-130). Transport request and response ports are excluded, so the internal stored and computed arbitration elements are the structural refs.

conceptual assets.concept: Switch lock-retention state -- whether the current A or B transaction stays owned until lock drops
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 111 forms locked_nxt from b_req_i.lock and a_req_i.lock, line 57 stores it in locked, and lines 88-92 and 100-104 use locked(0/1) to keep the busy owner driving stb from its request strobe until that request's lock deasserts instead of releasing only on x_rsp_i.ack. Integrity is established because this stored lock state changes when the switch returns to idle and which requester may continue a transaction; availability is the maintained locked-bus behavior until the implemented release condition occurs.

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway port-decode decision -- which downstream port receives the request
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 356-361 compute port_sel from req_i.addr and the enable/base/size generics, line 378 applies port_sel(i) to each forwarded request strobe, and line 416 also records the default X selection into keeper.halt. Integrity is established because this decision determines which downstream port receives the request and whether timeout handling treats the request as on the halt path. Transport ports are excluded, so the internal selector is the structural ref.

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway outstanding-transaction monitor state -- busy, lock, timeout counter, and halt
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 417-427 maintain the in-flight monitor: keeper.busy marks an outstanding request, keeper.lock stores the request lock, keeper.cnt counts cycles while busy, and keeper.halt remembers whether the request went to the fallback X port (416). This state decides whether the monitor resets, keeps waiting, times out, or releases on ack or lock drop (423-427). Integrity is established because timeout and release behavior depend on these stored values; availability is established because the state is created when req_i.stb starts a transaction (419-420) and cleared only by the implemented release conditions (425-427).

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway timeout error flag -- internal timeout event reported on the response
conceptual assets.reasoning: While busy, line 423 tests the counter MSB together with halt, line 424 sets keeper.err on timeout, and lines 400-401 OR keeper.err into rsp_o.ack and rsp_o.err. This is a reported error event, so integrity is established because corrupting it changes the visible response result; availability is also established because the flag is produced whenever the implemented timeout condition holds.

conceptual assets.concept: AMO RMW operation context -- saved phase, command, read data, and write operand for an in-flight atomic update
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_IDLE, lines 777-780 capture the AMO command and write operand and enter S_READ_WAIT; line 785 captures the read data; lines 787-801 step through EXECUTE, WRITE, WRITE_WAIT, and back to IDLE; and line 763 stores the complete non-transport arbiter record declared at lines 734-739. Integrity is established because sys_req_o.data/rw/stb (813, 815, 816), core_rsp_o.data (826), and the ALU computation (838-845, 850-853) all depend on this stored context. Availability is established because the context is preserved until the write and acknowledge sequence completes.

conceptual assets.concept: AMO computed write-back value -- the value written during the atomic update
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 838-845 compute alu_res from the saved command and operands, line 837 registers the chosen value, and line 813 sends alu_res on sys_req_o.data during S_WRITE and S_WRITE_WAIT. Integrity is established because this is the value actually written back for the atomic read-modify-write operation; availability is established because the registered result is produced on the execution clock edge and then used in the write phase.

conceptual assets.concept: LR/SC qualification and reservation state -- whether the request is reservation-based and whether a store-conditional may proceed
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 935 computes rvso when core_req_i marks an AMO with the reservation/conditional op class, lines 926-927 enter reservation state on a qualifying read-like request, lines 910-915 and 920-921 advance or clear the state on a store and on sys_rsp_i.ack, and line 944 gates sys_req_o.stb with state(1) for a qualifying store-conditional. Integrity is established because this decision and stored state define whether a store-conditional is forwarded and when the reservation is cleared; availability is established because the state transitions follow the qualifying request and acknowledge conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: Store-conditional failure result -- reported failure of a suppressed SC
conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 957 sets sc_fail when a qualifying store-conditional arrives without state(1), line 963 ORs sc_fail into core_rsp_o.ack, and line 964 ORs sc_fail into response data bit 0. This is a reported success/failure decision, so integrity is established because it changes the visible LR/SC result; availability is established because the failure flag is produced whenever the implemented condition holds.
